Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Person examining a corn ear in a still-green field
- The ear husks appear notably bleached/whitened/dried
- The rest of the plant foliage remains green
- The ear appears to have mold/rot with grayish discoloration

**Key diagnostic feature:** Bleached husks while the rest of the plant remains green is the hallmark symptom of Diplodia ear rot, which distinguishes it from other ear rots. The Diplodia reference images show the same pattern - white to grayish mold on ears with bleached husks on otherwise green plants.

**Ruling out other ear rots:**
- Gibberella: would show pinkish-red mold starting at the tip
- Fusarium: would show white-pink cottony mold on scattered kernels
- Aspergillus: would show olive-green powdery mold
- Trichoderma: would show dark green mold
- Common smut: would show distinctive fleshy galls
